label: Space as relative order of coexistence: Leibniz’s relational account in Third Paper §4: space…
term: space as relative order of coexistence
definition: Leibniz’s relational account in Third Paper §4: space concerns the order of coexisting bodies, rather than an independently placed absolute container. His §5 identifies the internally undifferentiated relocation cases on that account. This is not defined as merely equality of one measured distance table.
note: OPEN declaration-completion boundary (2026-11-09): the original reading does not specify a carrier of complete spatial data or an equivalence criterion. Concrete alternatives needing selection are pairwise unsigned distances (reflection-insensitive), oriented displacement data (orientation-sensitive), betweenness/order without metric scale, or a richer coexistence structure including further physical data. These differ: equal distance data can preserve a reflection that signed displacement data distinguish; order alone can survive changes of distance. The allowed presentation changes also remain unspecified: common translations, rotations, reflections, similarities, arbitrary relational isomorphisms, and body relabelings are different scopes. One must specify whether bodies retain fixed identities, whether empty configurations are admitted, and whether sameness is isomorphism of relational structures or literal equality of their representations (or equality of quotient classes under a specified action).
